newsitem.title: USA: Blue chips up but investors wary ahead of jobs data.
newsitem.headline: Blue chips up but investors wary ahead of jobs data.

text.p: A handful of stocks, including International Business Machines Corp., led the blue-chip market higher Thursday, but investors were tentative ahead of Friday's February employment data.
At 1 p.m. EST, the Dow Jones industrial average was up 13.09 points at 6,958.94 after soaring 93 points on Wednesday.
In the broader market, advancing issues led declines 12-10 on active volume of 312 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The shares of oil and financial companies accounted for most of the market's strength, while technology stocks were mostly weaker.
First Albany Corp.'s chief investment officer Hugh Johnson, said the strength in these two sectors was an anomaly.
"If you back away from the oils and the financials, you get the impression that the market is simply on hold until we see what the employment data tomorrow show," he said.
Oil stocks drew strength from a Bear Stearns upgrade of three major oil services companies to buy from attractive -- Halliburton Co., Schlumberger Ltd. and Varco International Inc.
Halliburton was up 1-1/2 at 68-3/8, Schlumberger rose 1-3/8 at 107-3/8 and Varco was up 1-1/8 at 25-3/4.
The financial sector got a shot in the arm from merger news involving Great Western Financial Corp. and Washington Mutual Savings Bank.
Great Western, trying to fend off a hostile takeover bid by A.H. Ahmanson and Co., said Thursday it agreed to be acquired by Washington Mutual for $6.6 billion.
Great Western climbed 1-3/4 to 46-3/4, and Washinton Mutual was down 3/8 at 52-7/8.
Bond traders were cautious ahead of the jobs data, and the key 30-year Treasury bond lost 13/32, while its yield rose to 6.86 percent from Wednesday's close of 6.83 percent.
Peggy Farley, chief executive officer at Amas Securities said despite the looming employment data, the primary concerns of investors remained macroeconomic.

"People are concerned about exchange rates and their impact on the continued growth of our economy, how long-term interest rates will impede growth and whether companies will continue to top the record increases they been reporting," she said.
Among special situations, Alex. Brown said it cut is rating on Atmel Corp. to buy from strong buy. Atmel's stock fell 1-1/2 to 31-1/8.
The Nasdaq Composite index was off 9.47 points at 1,319.62. The American Stock Exchange index slipped 0.40 to 600.48.
